reviewer: /root, independent informed AI content reviewer; not the task author
scope: Full DE/EN task, solution and scoring text for indices 0-8; eleven current whole-goal positive-evidence profiles (German); nine native candidate contexts and their secured goal texts. No acceptance of tasks 9-26, CQR, projection placement or classroom effectiveness.

rows.contentAnalysis: Microscopic vector sums 0,+4,-8 and before/during/after material histories jointly assess both whole-goal expectations; reversal is an additional transfer.
rows.counteranswer: A response calling both samples permanent only from the in-field reading fails the persistence criterion.

rows.contentAnalysis: Charge-sign reversal changes cancellation from horizontal to vertical components at P; negative radial fields, inverse-square scaling and spherical exterior limits are assessed.
rows.counteranswer: Adding field magnitudes instead of vectors, or inferring interior fields from exterior equality, fails separate required criteria.

rows.contentAnalysis: Positive and negative charges, transverse initial motion, slowing and reversal consistently distinguish force, trajectory and opposite energy changes.
rows.counteranswer: Claiming all kinetic energy vanishes at vx=0 despite vy>0 fails the trajectory/energy transfer.

rows.contentAnalysis: The sign inference, 30-degree force magnitude, parallel/perpendicular limits, controlled m/v/B changes and ambiguous unknown m/v case cover both claimed goals.
rows.counteranswer: Treating a radius of 2r as unique proof of double mass fails the explicitly uncontrolled-comparison criterion.

rows.contentAnalysis: The two particles and new double-mass/double-charge ion test separate radius and period scalings; relativistic and oblique entry limits are explicit.
rows.counteranswer: Doubling the period when only speed doubles, or applying the full-speed circle radius at 40 degrees, fails the relevant transfer.

rows.contentAnalysis: Parallel and perpendicular components, limiting paths, independent field reversal and parallel-velocity reversal diagnose which helical features actually change.
rows.counteranswer: Reversing the physical axial motion merely because B reverses fails the separate-reversal criterion.

rows.contentAnalysis: Acceleration, velocity selection and analysis are separated. Negative charge reverses both selector forces; analysis-field reversal and 1:2:1 m/|q| ratios remain consistent.
rows.counteranswer: Calling identical detector locations unique mass measurements fails the explicit charge/mass ambiguity criterion.

rows.contentAnalysis: Measured/set/inferred quantities are distinguished. Two independent tube settings determine specific charge; a separately supplied elementary charge is needed for mass.
rows.counteranswer: Treating the luminous radius as a direct mass reading fails the evidence-chain and independent-information criteria.

rows.contentAnalysis: Operating tables distinguish cyclotron and synchrotron. The new species changes m/|q|, the rigidity bound excludes both machines, and relativistic synchronism is explicitly limited.
rows.counteranswer: Claiming that a synchrotron automatically evades the same field/radius limit fails the quantitative feasibility criterion.

findings.finding: A separate total-score cap is not a separately enforced field of the runtime assessment contract. With 4-point steps and a max-minus-2 threshold, omitting a 2-point transfer can still meet the step sum threshold.
findings.requiredRepair: Apply an explicit maximum of 1/4 within each affected step when any essential statement or transfer of that step is omitted or replaced by a misconception. The ordinary sum then stays below the threshold. Retain equivalent valid methods and minor-error treatment.

findings.finding: A point 3a from two different spherical centres does not establish equal vector directions. The intended comparison needs the same centre in separate experiments.
findings.requiredRepair: Specify separate arrangements with each centre at the origin and the same observation point (3a,0), in DE and EN.

findings.finding: Case B does not fix the perpendicular velocity azimuth, whereas the answer assumes initial +x to give an absolute +y force.
findings.requiredRepair: Explicitly give initial v_perp along +x in both languages; retain the independent field and axial-velocity reversals.

findings.finding: Run B yields 1.76047728495281e11 C/kg; the four-significant-digit solution should read 1.760e11, not 1.761e11.
findings.requiredRepair: Correct both language solutions; no stimulus or scoring-threshold change is needed.
